title: Statistical Analysis of Structural and Compositional Distributions in Bulk Materials with Nanodomains via Combined 4D-STEM and STEM-EELS
content: Although a single-phase material with a homogeneous microstructure is ideal for studying certain properties, in many cases, multi-phase materials with coherently grown and interwoven nanodomains exhibit unique properties that make them valuable for various applications, including energy storage [1-2], piezoelectricity [3] and metal-alloy hardening [4]. Engineering multi-phase materials is often much more intricate than single-phase materials due to the inherent variety of microstructures. To optimize the properties of multi-phase materials, it is crucial to understand and precisely control nanodomain microstructures, necessitating characterization of nanoscale structural and compositional distributions.
